title: A Room of One's Own
author: Virginia Woolf
summary: Virginia Woolf considers why so few women wrote famous works in the past. She argues that a woman needs money and a room of her own to write fiction, and imagines a sister of Shakespeare whose talent was wasted.
readIf: you like essays on literature, gender and creative freedom with a distinct voice.
skipIf: you want a systematic argument rather than a wandering, fictionalized lecture.
